These Gap Covers definitely keep crumbs or spills or anything else from falling and getting into the cracks between the counter and stove...food, pot holders, towels, utensils....I love this aspect and am very happy about that! My only issue with them is, they are always spotted or smeared unless I clean them carefully by hand and hand dry them thoroughly.  If I toss them into the dishwasher, they come out spotted all over...and the spots don't want to wipe off and I must hand wash them anyway. If I wipe them off while wiping the counter...spots.  I can wash them by hand and dry them with a very good lint free kitchen towel and I must take great pains to dry without leaving spots. Quite a bit of time spent on keeping them looking nice. I have a beautiful new kitchen with shiny new black appliances including a glass top stove...which I keep spotless and sanitized when I'm not cooking/baking....the entire kitchen come clean with ease except for these covers...I have to work with them a lot to keep their spots and streaks from taking away from the neat clean look of the kitchen when it's not in use.  I don't mind the covers getting dirty...I bought 2 sets to compensate with their getting dirty often. But they get dirty so easily, and then don't clean up so well. I love to cook & bake for  family/friends.  I have plenty of items to clean, which is fine...they can all go in the dishwasher  and come out 1 hour later looking great...except for these little covers. I love the purpose

Sure glad I got this thing on sale, because if I'd paid 30 bucks for this piece of crap I'd be pissed!!! I really just wanted the collapsible cone, which is fine. Smaller than I anticipated but whatever it's only for backpacking anyway. The packaging....wow. I would not pick this package up off the shelf! Good thing for Brooklyn ice company that Amazon doesn't show packaging or have shelves. The cup has mysterious hooks on the side that would suggest a handle but there is none. The cup itself is so flimsy, I would never dream of trying to pick it up full of hot coffee! The little saucer thing...pointless. I guess it fits on the brim of the cup but again, see above re: how flimsy the cup is. The spoon....what on earth? Why does it have a hand on one end? The spoon and the hand both come right off of the shaft...they are not attached in any way. The actual spoon part is the flimsiest thing yet. In any case...the cone thing will do and the rest is going in the trash.
Awesome collapsible coffee cup! Really adorable, durable and works well. I love that it's so compact and that I can take it anywhere... really a great buy!

Better than I expected for the price. Mine still had some sort of membrane across where the holes in the dripper should be, but i just used a sharp knife to punch them out and it worked perfectly. I use number 2 cone filters in it- I don't make coffee in the included cup, I actually use that for pouring the hot water into the dripper (which I have sitting on my regular coffee cup). I'm a full time student (hence the need for lots of coffee) and a backpacker, so this is perfect for both of those things.
The Silicon wasn't really stable enough to stay upright so I was nervous to pour hot water into the filter. Cute concept though.

I bought this set mainly for the collapsible coffee filter holder. I do not use the cup or the spoon right now, but have kept them because you never know when things like that can be handy. The collapsible filter holder is perfect for camping. You do need some sort of paper filter of your choice to go along with it, I use the bowl shaped paper filters and gently stuff it down into the funnel for a secure fit. It holds just enough grounds for a travel mug amount of strong coffee. Pour hot water over the grounds in the funnel for a fresh cup of coffee. Washes easily with soap and water. Packs down flat to fit in a backpack, purse, or RV cupboard.
I do wish there was some way to see through the filter holder base, so that you can monitor the amount of water in the cup - but that's a minor concern. To make sure I'm not overfilling my mug, I pour water into the travel mug first as measuring cup then heat it up in my electric kettle. Works well! I've used this every morning while camping so far this year, a handful of times and love it.
This is so clever and I love it for travel as I want to make my own coffee.
